hypothesis: The catalog's single-accumulator first pass with a four-vector equality search measured 4.3046e-7 seconds, while four-accumulator variants paired with one- or eight-vector searches measured 5.2660e-7 and 4.5678e-7 seconds. Those results do not isolate the interaction. This candidate pairs four independent minimum accumulators with the four-vector search to test whether reducing first-pass dependency chains helps without losing the search loop's observed benefit. It preserves signed comparisons, earliest-match order, and tail handling; random and decreasing inputs may still differ in second-pass work.
notes: The implementation uses AVX-512F intrinsics already present in the supplied candidate and keeps its target attribute. The campaign context identifies GCC 14.2 and an AMD EPYC 9654 target; no commands or local build were run, so compilation and correctness remain for the controller to verify before timing. Historical timings are not measurements of this candidate.
transformations: Change the first-pass minimum reduction to four independent AVX-512F accumulators over groups of four vectors, then combine accumulators and process remaining vectors and scalar tail.
Unroll the second-pass equality search across four vectors; examine vector masks in index order and use the lowest set lane to preserve earliest-index ties.
Retain bounds-safe vector remainder and scalar-tail paths, including nonpositive sizes and INT32 extrema.
